# Row snocone-ladder-top-rung-census-from-the-snocone-manual-is-the-score (hq_P lane, seat10, 2026-09-04):
#   Lon 2026-09-03 20:45: 100% = 100% of the industry standard. Snocone has no public conformance suite, so
#   the reference censused into this ladder IS the standard and the ladder green to its top IS the score.
# SCHEMA is hq_T's shared eight-column one (row ladder-forms-column-and-forms-check-every-declared-form-and-
# pair-has-a-witness): RUNG CONSTRUCT REFERENCE FORMS PAIRS WITNESS_ORIGIN STATUS NOTE. FORMS is |-separated,
# one entry per form the reference lists; PAIRS is |-separated lower-rung CONSTRUCT slugs this construct must
# be combined with in the combinations phase (empty everywhere below -- isolation phase only, no combinations
# cut yet). Expected origins: isolation ladder__<rung>_<construct>_<form>.
# TWO REFERENCES, NOT ONE, AND THEY DISAGREE WITH EACH OTHER ON PURPOSE:
#  (a) corpus/tests/snocone/report.md -- Andrew Koenig's original 1985 USENIX paper (cited as "report.md:LINE").
#      This is THE reference for statement-level control flow (if/while/do/for/procedure/struct) and for the
#      language's own self-description, per this row's GOAL text.
#  (b) .github/ARCH-LANGUAGES.md sec SNOCONE (cited as "ARCH-LANGUAGES.md:LINE") -- the snobol4ever DERIVED
#      dialect SCRIP actually implements, which the project's own current architecture doc states in one
#      sentence: "Andrew Koenig's .sc self-host operator set, minus && / || / %, plus C-style structured
#      control flow, plus SPITBOL space-as-concat." Expression semantics are SPITBOL's (ARCH-LANGUAGES.md
#      Reference spec, SPITBOL Manual ch.15/17/18/19), NOT Koenig's -- concatenation is a bare space, not &&;
#      there is no ||; comparison is EQ()/NE()/LT()/... predicate CALLS, not infix ==/!=/<... (Koenig's own
#      infix comparison table at report.md:483 does NOT describe what SCRIP implements: :==: etc were REMOVED
#      from the language entirely 2026-08-24, s272, per ARCH-LANGUAGES.md's own section on it -- citing
#      report.md there would be citing a table that describes a syntax error). Every row below cites (a) for
#      the CONCEPT and (b) for the ACTUAL SPELLING wherever they diverge; NOTE says so explicitly per row.
#      Keyword check: the self-hosting snocone.sc (/home/resources/SNOCONE.zip) uses `procedure`, matching (a);
#      SCRIP's lexer (snocone_lex.c) once mapped only `function`; it maps BOTH since 6643087d8/c21ef5fce and
#      `procedure` is a graded form as of rung19 (2026-09-13) -- see rung19 NOTE and FINDING-2026-09-03-seat12-snocone-master-70-of-273-reds-were-the-wrong-instrument
#      -real-board-is-7-of-206.md Class A (procedure keyword: zero implementation, 5 corpus entries affected).
# RUNGS 00-09 ARE ALREADY BUILT, ABSORBED, AND GREEN (test_snocone_ladder.sh --to 9: 20/20 PASS both modes,
# measured 2026-09-04 tree SCRIP=2cd69baa corpus=e351e9a4c) -- their RUNG NUMBERS AND ORDER ARE SUNK, absorbed
# under origins `ladder__rungNN_<slug>__ladder__rungNN_<slug>` (doubled name; NOT a grading defect -- see
# FINDING-2026-09-04-hq_T-snocone-and-rebus-ladder-origins-are-doubled-because-their-rungs-were-absorbed-one
# -file-per-rung.md -- the doubling is cosmetic, lib_ladder.sh's population rule and the CSV `family` column
# both still resolve correctly; renaming to fix the cosmetics is a SEPARATE, more delicate row per that
# FINDING's own caution, not attempted here). Do NOT renumber 00-09 to match manual order more closely: that
# would require re-absorbing under new origin names, which the builder's drop-detector treats as DROP+ADD and
# refuses without `--allow-drop-origin` named per old origin (same FINDING). Their internal order therefore
# does NOT strictly track report.md's section order; new ground (rung10+) does, as closely as a census made in
# one sitting can manage.
# RUNGS 10+ ARE DECLARED, NOT YET BUILT ONTO THE GRADED LADDER: every WITNESS_ORIGIN citing a `ladder/prog/*.sc`
# path is REAL, EXISTING SOURCE (corpus/tests/snocone/ladder/prog/, ~70 files, informally hand-tested before
# this row and carrying a NATIVE_STATUS verdict in the old corpus/tests/snocone/ladder/LADDER.tsv this file
# supersedes) that has NOT been absorbed into ALL.sc/ALL.csv under the `ladder__rungNN_<slug>_<form>` naming
# the graded runner requires -- so none of it is on the master or gradeable by test_snocone_ladder.sh yet. Old
# NATIVE_STATUS=FAIL rows are carried into NOTE below as known defects, not guesses: whoever builds a rung
# forward should expect those specific forms to expose real bugs (stays RED, filed as a class row on its rung
# per THERE IS NO XFAIL -- Lon 2026-09-03), not chase a green that was never there.
# ⛔ `ladder/prog/*.sc` (cited below as prior art / reference material) IS NOT MEANT FOR MECHANICAL ABSORPTION:
# ladder/KEEP.md rules it a deliberately-standalone diagnostic/bug-hunting harness (bespoke oracle per probe,
# some stdin-driven, its whole job is to carry open FAILING entries) and explicitly says folding it into the
# banner-block suite format "would be inappropriate, not just extra work." Rungs 00-09 were NOT built by

Not absorbed as a graded witness, same PASS/FAIL/NOBUILD gap as rungs 10/11's REFUSE cases. column1: rung13
column3: report.md:591-603 if (expression) statement1 [else statement2]
column8: all three forms witnessed+absorbed+green (m3+m4). Confirmed rung12's D5 caveat GENERALIZES to plain if/else with NO user-visible label: `scrip --transpile | sbl -bf` on all three forms reproduces the same spurious-blank-OUTPUT= artifact from the synthesized Lendif_*/Lelse_* labels (verified directly on all three, not assumed) even though the source has no label the user wrote. Hand-cut idiomatic SPITBOL used instead (KEEP.md fallback): the label shares its line with the next real statement where one follows, or sits as a bare trailing label immediately before END where none does (confirmed side-effect-free, unlike the transpiler's synthesized `OUTPUT =` dummy) -- cross-checked byte-exact against native --run AND --compile before trusting. ⭐ THIS RUNG'S REQUIRED REFUSE CASE (verified, not contrived): `if` without parens around its condition (`if GT(x,3) { OUTPUT='big'; }`) is a hard parse error (rc=1, "snocone parse error: syntax error") -- Koenig's own grammar requires them. Not absorbed as a graded witness, same PASS/FAIL/NOBUILD gap as rungs 10-12's REFUSE cases. ⭐ QA correction, verified not assumed: infix `x > 3` as an if-CONDITION parses and runs correctly (rc=0) -- the earlier claim that Koenig's infix comparison operators are a blanket "REMOVED, hard parse error" (2026-08-24 s272 ruling, cited in this baton's own QA section) does not hold inside an if-condition specifically; not this row's file to correct (out of scope), flagging for whoever owns that ruling. Also confirmed: braces are OPTIONAL around a single if-body statement (`if (GT(x,3)) OUTPUT='big';` parses/runs identically to the braced form) -- witnesses here use braces throughout for consistency with the if_else/elif forms; bracelessness is not a separately declared form.

REQUIRED REFUSE CASE (verified): `while` without parens around its condition (`while LE(i,5) { ... }`) is a hard parse error (rc=1, "snocone parse error: syntax error"), same shape as rung13's -- Koenig's grammar requires them for while too. Not absorbed as a graded witness, same PASS/FAIL/NOBUILD gap as prior rungs' REFUSE cases. do-while (report.md:619-629) is a SEPARATE declared rung (15), not a form of this one -- Koenig documents them as two distinct statements, not one construct with an optional leading execution.

column1: rung15
column3: report.md:619-629 do statement while (expression)
column8: witnessed+absorbed+green (m3+m4); two cases in one witness (multi-iteration i=1..3, and the load-bearing run-at-least-once case: i=10 with LT(i,0) false from the start still prints 'once' exactly once -- the one behavior that actually distinguishes do-while from while, per prior-art ctl_dowhile.sc's own choice of cases). Cross-checked byte-exact against native --run AND --compile. REQUIRED REFUSE CASE (verified): `do STMT while EXPR` without parens around the trailing condition is a hard parse error (rc=1), same shape as rungs 13-14 -- third rung running with this exact REFUSE shape, worth expecting again on rung16 (for) rather than re-discovering. ⭐ Reinforces this sitting's QA correction (see rung13's NOTE): infix `term <= 3` tested directly as a do-while condition also parses and runs correctly (confirmed via a throwaway probe, not part of the graded witness) -- report.md's OWN Introduction worked example (report.md:181-187) uses this exact infix spelling (`while (term <= 1000)`), which is further evidence the s272 "blanket removed" ruling is too broad, not evidence of a regression.

column1: rung18
column3: NOT IN KOENIG -- report.md's Statements section (582-681) has no switch/case at all. SCRIP DIALECT EXTENSION (TT_CASE grammar node; old ladder marks switch and switch-default both PASS)
column8: both forms witnessed+absorbed+green (m3+m4), 4/4, minted 2026-09-13 by hq_I under MODE NONET. Refs ORACLE-CUT from hand-written SPITBOL twins (sbl -bf), the IDENT-chain lowering ARCH-LANGUAGES.md:657 names, with every case arm jumping to a shared ESAC label to encode ARCH-LANGUAGES.md:629 'no fall-through; implicit break at end of each case'. ⭐ THE SEMANTICS CAME FROM THE SPEC, NOT FROM SCRIP: SPITBOL has no switch, so the twin encodes what the dialect DECLARES and a disagreement would have been a real red, not a ref to adjust. Both witnesses add a trailing OUTPUT='after' the old ladder/prog/ctl_switch*.sc prior art lacks -- it is load-bearing, proving control resumes after the switch and did not fall through into default; without it a fall-through bug in the last case before default would grade green. Honesty proof: corrupting simple_output_215's ref reds exactly that witness in BOTH modes, sibling stays green. ⛔ TRAP MET AND CURED HERE, GENERALIZES TO EVERY LANGUAGE: the --twin-equivalence prose is absorbed INTO the graded block and IS scanned by util_build_master_suite.py's feature-flag deriver (goto_success is literally `1 if ':S(' in t`), so a comment that SPELLS an operator sets that flag on a witness whose code has none -- the first draft of switch_case's prose said IDENT(e,v) followed by the success-goto operator and carried goto_success=1 into ALL.csv. Reworded to name the operator instead of spelling it. That is this digest's own g_zeta_mode lesson WITH THE OBSERVER MOVED: the filed warning is about a global READ only by emitted code, invisible to a grep for a read; this is a global WRITTEN only by emitted code, invisible to a patch of the writer. A cure keyed on HOW the value arrives cannot work when the arrival is not in the compiler's own sources. THE CURE IS BLIND TO THE WRITER BY CONSTRUCTION: rt_kw_seed_defaults (keyword init, which both modes reach) arms an on_exit handler that consults kw_code at exit however it got there. on_exit AND NOT atexit, because on_exit is handed the exit status: the handler fires only on status 0, so a program that already failed keeps its own rc -- verified, a &STLIMIT error with &CODE=5 set still exits 1, and a parse error still exits 1. ⛔ A SECOND DEFECT IN MY OWN CURE, CAUGHT BY GRADING m4 RATHER THAN REASONING: _exit skips stdio, so the first cure printed the right rc and LOST THE PROGRAM'S OUTPUT in m4 (rc=3, stdout empty). fflush before _exit. m3 hid it, which is why a both-modes grade is not optional.
